speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for presenting with hematuria and right flank pain. To determine the cause, are you currently experiencing fever, nausea, or visible blood clots in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 42-year-old Caucasian male. The patient reports experiencing visible blood in his urine accompanied by discomfort in his right flank. He denies any recent trauma to the area. He mentions a series of urinary tract infections over the past few years but has not been on renal dialysis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Kidney Stones (Nephrolithiasis).

Given your history of recurrent urinary tract infections and the classic presentation of visible hematuria with right flank pain, I need to confirm if you have passed any stones recently or if the pain comes in waves. REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis with microscopy and urine culture. REQUEST TEST: Renal Ultrasound or Non-contrast CT Abdomen/Pelvis.
